newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo vows to stay economic course.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo vows to stay economic course.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on Wednesday pledged to maintain Mexico's current fiscal and monetary policy, saying he would not bend to partisan political pressure for changes.
"We will continue on this road," Zedillo said during a trip to the northern industrial state of Nuevo Leon, one of the most prosperous in Mexico.
"There won't be any particular political interests, no political propaganda, that will cut short this policy, which is a correct policy and one that we are going to sustain," he said.
His comments appeared directed at opposition party calls to reduce the sales tax, also known as the value-added tax, from its current level of 15 percent.
Zedillo also has fended off pressure to alter an austere economic programme that he says has been key to pulling Mexico out of its worst recession in 60 years.

Leaders of the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) and conservative National Action Party (PAN) have called for reductions in the sales tax since Zedillo's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) lost its absolute majority in Congress in the July 6 elections.

The opposition parties have indicated they may join forces in the lower house in a bid to reduce the unpopular tax. But any effort may find opposition in the Senate, which is still controlled by the PRI.
Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz on Tuesday sharply criticised calls for reducing the sales tax, saying it would create havoc with the country's finances.
